risks.note: The Company had no revenue from operations for the year ended March 31, 2021 and states it has no manufacturing facility. The segment note records that the Company has only finance income and therefore no separate reportable business segment, leaving no operating base from which to service obligations.

The auditors report that accounting vouchers, business files, sales and purchase invoices and other audit evidence were not available for review, that the Statutory Registers required under the Companies Act, 2013 were not produced, and that the audit was carried out on an 'as and where' basis from few available records. This limits the reliability of reported balances.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company underwent CIRP admitted by NCLT Mumbai on June 04, 2021; the Resolution Plan filed by M/s. PP Metallix Limited was approved by NCLT on December 06, 2023. Continuity of the Company as a going concern depends on successful implementation of that plan, and the auditors note that the impact of the approved resolution plan was not taken into consideration in preparing the financial statements, a stated deviation from IND AS 10.
- The Company had no revenue from operations for the year ended March 31, 2021 and states it has no manufacturing facility. The segment note records that the Company has only finance income and therefore no separate reportable business segment, leaving no operating base from which to service obligations.
- The auditors report that accounting vouchers, business files, sales and purchase invoices and other audit evidence were not available for review, that the Statutory Registers required under the Companies Act, 2013 were not produced, and that the audit was carried out on an 'as and where' basis from few available records. This limits the reliability of reported balances.
- The auditors draw attention to trade receivables, loans and advances and other financial assets outstanding for more than one year that management has treated as good and recoverable with no provision made, and state they are unable to comment on recoverability, a stated deviation from IND AS 107.
- Investments are carried at the previous year's book value with no provision made on account of fair market value; the auditors are unable to comment on their recoverability and fair value, a stated deviation from IND AS 113.
- The Company did not file forms or returns with the Registrar of Companies, Regional Director, Central Government, the Tribunal, Court or statutory authorities such as TDS, PF and ESI during the year under review. No Internal Auditor was appointed and no internal audit was carried out under Section 138. Contingent liabilities include penalties levied by the exchange and a sales tax assessment. The Secretarial Auditor's qualifications relate to these delays and non-compliances.
- During CIRP the powers of the Board stood suspended and SEBI LODR regulations 17 to 21 on the Board and its committees were not applicable. The reconstituted Board states it cannot verify directorships and committee memberships held as at March 31, 2021, could not obtain Code of Conduct affirmations, could not carry out board performance evaluation, and could not comprehensively assess independent-director confirmations.
- Claims by financial creditors, operational creditors and employees admitted in the CIRP remain unaccounted pending plan implementation, with book balances to be re-cast on successful implementation; the auditors also cannot verify the nil disclosure of dues to micro and small enterprises. Separately, the Company's application for listing of shares arising out of a warrant conversion remains pending with the stock exchange and marked for re-submission, though management recorded them as issued and converted.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Complete implementation of the NCLT-approved Resolution Plan under the supervision of the Monitoring Agency and preserve the Company's status as a going concern.
- Re-establish corporate governance practices after reconstitution of the Board, including re-adoption and implementation of the Code of Conduct and a structured succession-planning framework.
- Strengthen the compliance framework and internal controls and regularise pending statutory filings and non-compliances identified by the Secretarial Auditor.
